parsed.study_design: Historical case study based on systematic archival and documentary review
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents, households, municipal water consumers, and industrial users in Barreiro, Setúbal; evidence drawn from municipal service reports, archival records, legislation, parliamentary materials, institutional studies, and private company records spanning approximately the 1930s–1990s.
parsed.exposure: Construction and municipalization of the public water-supply network, compulsory household connection and minimum-consumption charges, income-based exemptions and tariffs, state financing and regulation, and policies governing private groundwater extraction.
parsed.outcome: Water-service access and consumption, affordability and nonpayment, household connection and consumer contracts, availability of greater water volumes, and longer-term groundwater overexploitation and contamination affecting supply.
parsed.rationale: The Methods section (p. 141) identifies a historical case-study design using systematic review of archival materials, municipal annual reports, legislation, parliamentary records, institutional reports, and private company documents. The section “Nuevos impuestos, sobreexplotación y contaminación” reports empirical affordability and access outcomes, including unpaid water bills, acknowledged inability to pay, income-based exemptions, new consumer contracts, and consumption trends (pp. 144–147). The conclusions link mandatory payment and connection rules to constrained household choice and economic dependence while also documenting expanded service and resource pressures (pp. 148–149). The Spanish full text is sufficiently comprehensible for assessment and extraction.
